title: Nonprofits report heavy application and reporting effort and late payments on government contracts and grants

history.reason: Signal from Urban Institute national survey; data are from 2012.

description: In a 2013 national survey, about 75 percent of nonprofits with government funding said application and reporting complexity was a problem and 53 percent said late payments for services already provided were a problem.
customer_segment: Charitable nonprofits with $100,000+ in expenses holding government contracts or grants; small nonprofits are less likely to hold government funding.
context: Evidence is about 13 years old and covers 2012; still-current conditions are unverified.

evidence.text: For about 75 percent of surveyed nonprofits, the complexity and time required for applying and reporting on government contracts and grants was a problem.
For 53 percent, late government payments for services already provided were a problem.
Nonprofits with late-payment problems were significantly more likely to draw on reserves, borrow and cut programs.
Grant-and-contract administration software or services could reduce this effort for small nonprofits.

alternatives: Grant-management software, accounting systems, consultants: not investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: Only 17 percent of nonprofits with $100,000-$249,999 budgets hold government funding, limiting the number of small nonprofits affected.
The data are from 2012; conditions, payment practices and tools may have changed.

uncertainty: Unknown: current prevalence, dollar cost of the effort, who buys tools, willingness to pay, and existing product coverage.
open_questions: Do newer data (for example nonprofit sector surveys since 2020) show the same pattern?
Which payers and program types cause most delays?
next_actions: Find a post-2020 primary source on nonprofit government payment timeliness and reporting burden.
